title: Compact onboarding panes with doc links and contextual screenshots
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and deliver a compact, non-modal onboarding pane pattern that surfaces contextual doc links and inline screenshots at the point of friction in the Redwood Console. This ticket covers: (1) component anatomy and responsive layout for the pane and doc-link cards; (2) screenshot treatments and rules for when to auto-capture vs. upload mock images; (3) microcopy guidance for quickstarts and link priorities; (4) accessibility states and keyboard interactions; (5) handoff assets for engineering and content teams. Primary user flows: first-run (new org), first-use of Dedicated config, and when users open the Model Catalog route for the first time. Aim: reduce first-hour task time by 25% and increase doc click-through on key quickstarts by 40%.

design_decisions: Use a right-anchored pane (non-modal) instead of center modals to preserve user context and allow multitasking.
Doc links are prioritized: Quickstart steps > API reference > Troubleshooting. Keep link list to max 4 items to avoid clutter.
Inline screenshots default to annotated static PNGs; reserve auto-captured live screenshots for major releases only to control privacy and flakiness.
Accessibility: pane must be reachable via keyboard (tab focus order) and include ARIA roles: complementary + heading + list; focus trap only when user opens 'Guided mode'.
Animations are subtle (200ms ease) to reduce motion discomfort; provide PREFERS-REDUCED-MOTION fallback.
Collapsed state shows 1 short hint line + primary doc link; expanding reveals steps and screenshots.
Microcopy tone: concise, developer-focused, call-to-action oriented (verbs first) and include inline sample commands where appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens and component specs checked into Figma with responsive constraints and component variants.
Annotated screenshots for the three primary flows uploaded to Drive and linked in the PRD.
Interactive prototype demonstrating collapsed→expanded transitions for desktop and mobile.
Accessibility checklist validated: keyboard nav, ARIA roles, color contrast >= 4.5:1, reduced-motion support.
Hand-off package in Confluence includes copy snippets, link priority rules, and QA checklist for engineering.
Design review approval from PM (Janel Kim) and Eng lead (Rafael Gomes) recorded in comments.
